parsed.explanation: The dossier documents no trans-specific law, border practice, facility rule or violence against trans visitors; the operative restriction is a same-sex 'morality' offence (Art. 300/318) with disputed penalties of six months to five years, enforced episodically but genuinely — a 2022 prosecution and a June–December 2024 detention ending in conviction on 12 December 2024. A trans visitor is not targeted for presentation in any documented case, and 2023 saw no prosecutions, so exposure turns on conduct, a partner, or discretionary morality policing. Severity if detained is real: months of pretrial custody, poor prisons, no LGBTIQ organisation, no anti-discrimination recourse, widespread impunity. Societal stigmatisation is documented for LGBTQ people generally, not trans people specifically. Entry-document, screening, facilities and care practice are simply unsourced — open questions, not documented exposures.

entry_documents.exposure: No source addresses visa, passport marker, X-marker or screening treatment of trans visitors; unknown how a marker/presentation mismatch is handled at the border.
entry_documents.interaction: An unsourced stage; if a mismatch drew secondary inspection it would feed into the morality-law and detention machinery documented elsewhere.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Two women held June to December 2024 on a same-sex/morality basis, convicted and released with time served; pre-trial custody of months is documented practice. Custody conditions and placement by gender marker are not documented.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No LGBTIQ organisation exists to assist detainees; consular access not sourced.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A police stop escalating via a broad 'morality/unnatural acts' article can end in months of pre-trial custody without support infrastructure.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No documented rule on bathrooms, changing rooms, hospital wards or detention placement by gender marker; the dossier is silent.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Unresolved; absence of evidence here is not evidence of protective practice.

care_services.exposure: Trans-specific care and hormone access are unsourced; no anti-discrimination law covers service provision, and general LGBTQ discrimination in education and employment is recorded.
care_services.protection: None documented; 2012 Labour Code provides no protection.
care_services.interaction: A clinic encounter has no documented remedy route if refused or if identity is disclosed.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: The penal code frames same-sex conduct as contrary to morality or 'unnatural'; the government has repeatedly refused decriminalisation. No trans-specific criminal provision or state threat-framing of gender nonconformity is documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Police reported in 2023 that they did not incite or tolerate violence against LGBTQI+ people.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: The morality framing gives officers broad discretion; whether it is turned on presentation rather than conduct is undocumented.

minors_guardians.exposure: No source addresses a minor travelling with a guardian, age-dependent rules, schooling, or family/guardianship exposure for trans minors.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No documented violence against trans people and no trans-specific statistics; the 2023 report records no reported anti-LGBTQI+ violence. Widespread impunity is listed among major human-rights problems.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Police stated they do not incite or tolerate such violence.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: General impunity weakens any assumption that a complaint from a visibly trans visitor would be pursued.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No non-discrimination law, no legal gender recognition, no registered LGBTIQ organisation (association law chills registration), courts convicting under the morality article.
remedies_unknowns.protection: A formal appeal exists but no documented case of relief for LGBTQ defendants; one conviction was called a human-rights violation by an NGO.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Recourse is paper-thin and, under a hostile statute plus inefficiency, functioning institutions are a liability rather than a shield.

anchor_checks.comparison: Karthovia documents police systematically stopping trans visitors, seizing documents, hours of interrogation and fines. Nothing comparable is documented here: no trans visitor has been stopped for presentation, and enforcement is conduct-driven and episodic. Karthovia's targeting is documented and repeated; here it is absent from the record, so this jurisdiction is not below it, and the undocumented trans-specific exposures place it above.

Vesskar imposes a continuous universal exposure — linked biometric cards checked at banks, clinics and checkpoints — with documented detention, humiliation and care denial. Here no such continuous checkpoint regime reaches every visitor; the morality statute attaches to conduct and is enforced case-by-case, with 2023 showing no prosecutions. Similar severity if caught, materially lower frequency of exposure, so this rates above 0.45-A.

Kestrel Isles documents border officers routing trans travellers to secondary interview, luggage searches, refused admission and discretionary public-order grounds, with slow and rarely revised appeals. Those are documented traveller-facing practices at the entry stage. Here the entry stage is entirely unsourced, so this jurisdiction cannot claim Kestrel's workable (if humiliating) administrative pathway, but it also lacks documented refusals — it sits below on evidence.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller-facing record is thin but structurally unfavourable. The state criminalises same-sex conduct under a morality article whose penalty ranges from six months to five years across sources, has enforced it recently including months of pre-trial custody, refuses decarceration, permits no LGBTIQ organisation, and offers no anti-discrimination remedy; impunity is general. Against that, no trans visitor is documented as stopped, refused entry, denied facilities or attacked for presentation, 2023 saw no prosecutions, and police are recorded as not inciting violence. Societal stigmatisation is documented only for LGBTQ people in general, and 26% poll approval signals friction rather than organised hostility. Entry documents, screening, facilities and care are open questions, weighted lightly. The resulting exposure is episodic and conduct-dependent but severe when triggered, so the jurisdiction sits in the Elevated Risk band rather than at either extreme.
